messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: auth-service is reporting elevated token introspection failures (Auth0). 401s spiking across sessions. Alert A-3781.

PagerDuty: Paging Alex K (on-call).

Alex K: I'm on it. seeing 401s in traces for /api/session/introspect and console auth. Dashboard error rate ~12% for last 6m.

Sam T: same — noticed an uptick around 10:22 UTC, started around 10:18. Error payload from auth-proxy: 
```
{"status":401, "error":"invalid_token", "provider":"auth0", "request_id":"req_9a7f"}
```

Jordan L: quick check — Auth0 status page shows degraded performance: https://status.auth0.com/incidents/xyz-2026. They mention increased error rates for introspection.

Maya R: can we confirm it's upstream vs our network? curl from one of the auth-proxy pods to introspect endpoint: 
```bash
curl -v -X POST "https://auth0.example.com/oauth/introspect" -d "token=REDACTED"
* Connected to auth0.example.com (13.35.22.1) port 443 (#0)
> POST /oauth/introspect HTTP/1.1
> Host: auth0.example.com
> ...
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< Content-Type: application/json
< {"error":"invalid_request","error_description":"Service temporarily overloaded"}
```

Alex K: looks upstream. But we still need mitigation to reduce customer impact. Console (internal UI) calls failing for some users. ProductOps — any high-touch customers on support?

ProductOps: A few enterprise customers reported inability to log in to the console. No immediate P1 escalations yet but several support tickets.

Leah P: suggested mitigations in runbook: 1) enable cached-session fallback on auth-proxy, 2) temporarily relax SSO token enforcement for console routes, 3) increase local token-verification TTL. Which can we do quickly?

Alex K: I'll flip cached-session fallback first. command: 
```bash
# enable cached sessions (non-privileged routes)
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/auth-proxy ENABLE_CACHED_SESSIONS=true --record
```
Applying now.

SRE-oncall: Patch applied, rolling restart of auth-proxy pods. Watching pods come back.

Sam T: logs from auth-proxy after restart show fewer 401s on non-console web routes. Console still 401ing for some users (session renewal flow hits introspect).

Maya R: next step — relax SSO enforcement for the console route. We can allow bearer tokens signed by our fallback key for a small percentage of requests. I'll prepare a canary configuration.

Alex K: Do it, start at 10% traffic. Command: 
```bash
# add policy for console canary to accept fallback tokens
kubectl -n prod apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: auth-proxy-policies-canary
data:
  console-relax: |
    routes:
      - path: /console/*
        fallback_token_accept: true
        sample_rate: 0.1
YAML
```

Jordan L: Policy applied. Canary at 10%. Telemetry shows console failures dropped from 18%->7% for canary users.

ProductOps: Good — escalate to a notice to support and CS to proactively message affected customers.

Leah P: Also increasing local verification cache TTL to reduce introspect calls. 
```bash
redis-cli -h redis.prod INCRBY verify_cache_ttl 300  # add 5m
```
This will let our service reuse positive verifications.

Sam T: done. Monitoring shows introspect call rate down 35% and overall 401 rate lowered.

Alex K: Ok, rolling mitigations look effective. Next: contact Auth0 support for ETA and request priority incident. I opened a ticket and included traces + sample request ids. Ticket ID: AUTH0-7682.

Maya R: thumbs up. Also toggled canary to 50% for console since metrics stable.

SRE-oncall: Canary at 50%. No anomalies in latencies.

PagerDuty: Handoff reminder: Alex, your shift ends in 40m. Please hand off status.

Alex K: Handoff to Maya R. Current state: upstream Auth0 degraded (status incident), we've enabled cached-session fallback and relaxed console SSO for canary then 50%, increased verify cache TTL. Customer impact: ~3-5% residual login failures, console access largely restored for canary users. Monitoring dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/abc/auth-introspect. Postmortem: create INC-2026-17825.

Maya R: I'm taking on-call. Will keep an eye. Steps: 1) wait for Auth0 incident to resolve; 2) gradually rollback relax policy once stable; 3) prepare post-incident communication.

Jordan L: Do we need to rotate any keys or invalidate sessions afterward? Risk: cached positives might let in revoked tokens. Suggest setting a short TTL rollback plan.

Leah P: Good call — plan: once upstream stable, set verify_cache_ttl back to baseline over 10m and run a token revocation sweep for users who triggered security alerts. Create ticket: SEC-2026-421.

ProductOps: Opening customer comms draft for review. We'll soft-notify affected enterprise accounts and include workaround steps.

Alex K: Logging timeline and commands in the incident doc. Also request SRE on-call followup to add a circuit-breaker in auth-proxy to detect provider degraded state and more gracefully switch to fallback.

IncidentBot: Incident A-3781 marked: mitigated (working around upstream). Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring for regression.

Maya R: Will take 4-hour watch. If Auth0 doesn't provide ETA within 2 hours, escalate to vendor liaison + legal for contract SLA review.

Sam T: Notes for postmortem: - faster detection for introspect latency spikes - test cached-session fallback in staging - add observability for percent of requests using fallback tokens - update runbook to include canary % recommendations.

Jordan L: Created Jira: INC-2026-17825 (postmortem), SRE-2026-99 (circuit-breaker). Assignments: Alex -> incident writeup, Maya -> vendor escalation followup, Leah -> security sweep.

Maya R: Thanks team. I'll update status channel and the incident doc hourly. Leaving this thread for on-call handover.

Alex K: signing off. good catch everyone. :thumbsup:

SRE-oncall: Acknowledged handoff. Monitoring: continue to watch auth-introspect 401 rate and dashboard latency.

ProductOps: I'll coordinate customer comms and attach mitigation steps + timeline in support tickets.

(End of thread)
